subject.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses

question: After rebasing this lifecycle-sensitive Codex sandbox change, does the Codex/exec-server owner confirm that settling a stream failure while deferring terminal finalization to child close matches the upstream protocol contract?
rationale: The repository policy makes direct sibling-Codex source inspection mandatory for this integration boundary, and the supplied PR evidence cannot substitute for an owner-level contract decision on close ordering.

options.title: Audit and merge after refresh
options.body: Rebase, inspect the exact sibling Codex close/stream contract, and merge if the refreshed merge result preserves one terminal close and one lease finalization.

options.title: Pause for a narrower lifecycle design
options.body: Keep the PR open if the upstream contract expects a different stream-error terminal sequence or a separate owner-managed state transition.

recommendation.title: Audit and merge after refresh
recommendation.body: Rebase, inspect the exact sibling Codex close/stream contract, and merge if the refreshed merge result preserves one terminal close and one lease finalization.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context only establishes direct ownership of the proposed lifecycle implementation; a current-main Codex lifecycle owner should join the final decision after the required audit.
